THE BLUEPRINT TRAINING
Part 1 · How People Search
The Future of Search
THE BLUEPRINT
Part 1 · How People Search
GOOGLE IS TELLING US THEMSELVES...
Everyone WILL HAVE an agent. Agents WILL ENGAGE WITH OTHER agents.
Searches will be directed by a human, performed by agents.
Google’s information agents watch the web 24/7 and hand back a summary. Nobody scrolls the results page, so nobody clicks.
Agents build the shortlist, not rankings.
Google’s Agent2Agent standard (100+ backers) lets agents trade reviews, prices and availability. A business agents can’t read doesn’t make the list.
The website stops being where the deal happens.
Connected Apps put businesses inside AI Mode and Gemini. The traffic you used to report on is no longer the scoreboard.
Sources: Google I/O 2026 keynote · Linux Foundation (A2A) · Google Connected Apps Platform · mariehaynes.com

AI IS ALREADY CAPABLE OF DOING THE STRATEGY, deliverables and execution.
  • GPT-5.4 matched or beat professionals with about 14 years’ experience on 83% of expert tasks.
  • 100× faster and cheaper on those same tasks, counting model time and API cost only.
  • 12 hours = the length of expert work an AI agent can now finish on its own, doubling about every 7 months.
  • Delivery is already automated: audits, keyword research, content briefs, on-page fixes and reporting. AI can access websites and backends to make all of the changes that used to take hours.

OK…so...what do we do?
THE SEO agency’s 5 year roadmap
RIGHT NOW · 2026
SEO Only
  • Retainers sold on rankings and organic traffic
  • Deliverables are audits, content, links and a monthly report
  • Clicks are falling as AI Overviews answer the question
  • Clients start asking where the leads are
  • One channel, so one line in the client’s budget
YEAR 1 · 2027
Blended Search
  • Local Services Ads: verification, reviews, lead disputes
  • Google Ads on the high-intent money keywords
  • Map pack: Business Profile, categories, review velocity
  • Organic and AI answers: pages built to get cited
  • Call tracking and one report: cost per lead by channel
YEAR 2 · 2028
Full Service
  • Everything from year 1, plus paid social to reach people before they search
  • Website and conversion: landing pages, intake, speed
  • Email and CRM follow-up on every lead
  • One all-inclusive retainer and one revenue dashboard
  • Delivered with AI, managed by a small team of people
YEAR 3 AND BEYOND
Fractional CMO
  • You own the marketing plan and budget, not a channel
  • A seat in leadership meetings with the owner
  • You direct vendors, specialists and your own AI agents
  • Annual plan, quarterly roadmap, monthly scorecard
  • A handful of clients at high retainers
WHAT CHANGES
An SEO-only retainer
One retainer for the whole results page
A rankings report
Calls, forms and cost per lead
Organic traffic only
LSAs, Google Ads, Maps, organic and AI answers
Waiting 6 months for results
Paid leads in month one while organic builds
TRADITIONAL SEO IS NOT ENOUGH, YOU HAVE TO Own the whole page.
  • Strip down SEO to productized service. If it doesn't impact results, don't do it. Stripping down time allows to you deliver the service at a much lower cost. 

  • Integrate paid ads. Google Ads and Local Services Ads (now run inside Google Ads), plus call tracking on every number.

  • Repackage the offer. One retainer that covers the whole page, with ad spend billed separately.

  • Change the report. Lead with calls, forms and cost per lead by surface. Rankings move to the back.

  • Pilot with your three best clients for 90 days, then make it the only offer you sell.
Stage 1 · Blended Search
WHAT CHANGES
Four vendors and four invoices
One partner, one all-inclusive retainer
A report per channel
One dashboard tied to leads and revenue
A hire for every new service
AI systems run delivery, you run quality
Competing for one line in the budget
Owning the whole marketing budget
MOVE FROM A VENDOR TO ONE STOP SHOP 
  • List what each client buys from someone else. Website, paid social, email, CRO, video. That list is your growth plan.

  • Turn each service into an AI-run system before you sell it. Write the SOP, then build the agent that does the work.

  • Add one channel at a time. Paid social first, then website and conversion, then email and CRM follow-up.

  • Bundle it into one all-inclusive retainer with tiers. Take over the other vendors’ work at their renewal dates.

  • Report every channel in one dashboard tied to leads and revenue, not channel metrics.
Stage 2 · Full Service
WHAT CHANGES
Selling deliverables
Owning decisions and results
Reporting to a marketing manager
A seat at the owner’s table
Dozens of small clients
A handful of high-retainer clients
Doing the tasks yourself
Directing agents and specialists
THE ENTIRE MARKETING DEPARTMENT
  • Pick a niche and a client size that can afford a CMO retainer, and that you already know cold.

  • Move up the org chart. Sell to the owner, sit in leadership meetings, and own the marketing budget and plan.

  • Productize your strategy: an annual plan, a quarterly roadmap and a monthly scorecard every client gets.

  • Hand execution to AI agents and specialists you manage. Your job is direction, review and accountability.

  • Price on scope and outcomes, not hours. Cap your roster at a handful of clients.
